items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: But Guy Kelly was more musical, you know, reading man. Read more. That's how he stayed more with Papa Celestine.

ctx.x: What about Chris Kelly? Who did he have in his band? Do you remember any of those fellas at all?

No. Chris had so many of them. What about Guy Kelly? Do you remember any of the fellas? I did. His brother, well he worked with Papa Celestine a lot. He was, in other words, played second with Papa Celestine most of the time. What did you say about his brother?
Chris? Yeah. Didn't you say something about brother and Guy there?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: And after the line was a fella called Guy Kelly. Mm-hmm. The trumpet man. Fast, you know, fast, fast. He didn't know what I mean. He was, he was still a scambler.

ctx.x: Well after Arnold had passed, who were some of those other bands that you just splattered around with and stuff?

None in particular, like I said, Renee, Chris, Guy Kelly, he was with Celestine Warr, and the time he'd get work, you know. Split the band, I'd work in their place. I was mostly hired out like that. And one small orchestra, with myself, let me see Rochon, where he's living, he's preaching now.
